features.featureTitle: Replace the current screen flow in frontend/src/App.tsx with the new mini-game flow screens and navigation, using only client-side state transitions (no backend calls): (1) Game Intro, (2) Level 1, (3) Final Level, (4) Real Question, (5) YES Celebration, (6) Optional Extra-Cute Ending with Replay. The Replay action must restart the game from Game Intro (or Level 1) and reset any per-level counters/timers/messages.

Update the existing Intro screen UI to match the new Game Intro screen copy and primary action. User-facing text must be exactly:
- “Hi Anya 💕\nWelcome to a tiny game I made just for you.”
- “Your mission: find the NO button 😌”
Primary button label must be exactly: “🎮 Start Game”. Keep the screen mobile-first, centered, with a thumb-friendly bottom CTA area.

Implement Level 1 screen (“The Game Begins”) with the following exact user-facing header text at the top: “Level 1: Find the NO button ❌”. The screen must include animated distractions: hearts floating around, a teddy walking back and forth, and flowers popping in and out. Ensure animations are lightweight and mobile-optimized.

Implement the Level 1 “hidden NO button” mechanic: a real NO button appears for approximately 0.5 seconds, then disappears, and repeatedly relocates to new positions. The NO button must sometimes appear visually ‘behind’ (partially occluded by) one of the distraction elements: a teddy, a flower, or a chocolate. When the user taps the area where the NO button last appeared, the NO button must immediately move/hide again and trigger a light vibration (using the browser Vibration API when available).

Add Level 1 funny pop-up feedback messages that appear briefly after each miss/escape. Randomly select and display one of the following exact messages: “Nope 😜”, “Missed it!”, “It ran away!”, “Try again 😂”. After a few tries (define a consistent threshold, e.g., 4 misses), also show the exact progress line: “Hmm… this is harder than it looks 🤔”.

Implement the Final Level screen with the exact user-facing text: “Final Level: Last chance 😏”. The screen must show multiple fake tappable buttons with the exact labels: “NO?”, “Not this one”, “Almost!”. Each fake button must vanish when tapped. After the fake buttons sequence, the screen must clear and advance to the Real Question screen.

Implement the Real Question screen with slowed-down pacing/feel and soft music behavior: keep the global AudioToggle, but on this screen emphasize the ‘soft music’ moment by presenting the content in a calmer animation cadence (e.g., slower fades). User-facing text must be exactly two lines:
- “Okay Anya… no more games.”
- “Will you be my Valentine? 💝”
Render one clear primary button labeled exactly: “✅ YES 💕”. Do not render any NO button on this screen.

Update the YES celebration flow so that after tapping “✅ YES 💕” it (a) triggers confetti burst, (b) hearts explosion, (c) shows a teddy hugging a heart, then (d) displays the requested sweet messages one-by-one in order (each message visible clearly before the next appears):
1) “You are absolutely beautiful 🌸”
2) “I’m so grateful to have you in my life ❤️”
3) “Every moment with you means everything to me”
4) “Thank you for being you, Anya 🥰”
Then show the final line exactly:
“Happy Valentine’s Day 💕\nI’m really lucky to be with you.”

Add the optional Extra-Cute Ending screen after the celebration sequence that shows a teddy holding a sign with the exact text: “Best Valentine Ever 🧸❤️” and a single button labeled exactly: “Replay the game 😄”.

Apply the requested mini-game visual style adjustments across the new game screens: pastel colors (pink, peach, lavender), soft bouncing animations, cute characters (teddy, hearts, flowers), and mobile-first one-hand-friendly layout (big tap areas, no zooming required).

Incorporate the uploaded images into the app as static assets (stored under frontend/public/assets/generated or an equivalent static public path) and use them where appropriate for teddy/valentine-game visuals, ensuring any backgrounds that look like checkerboards are removed or avoided so assets appear clean on pastel backgrounds.
